chapter_title: 第138章 獻給所有人的歌

segments.title: 第138章 獻給所有人的歌
segments.content:
A Song for Everyone

"This Polaroid of yours, where did you buy it?"

While queuing for food, Ying Chanxi pretended to be making small talk and asked Li Luo.

"At a specialty store diagonally across from the residential complex," Li Luo said. "Why do you ask?"

"Oh, it's nothing, just asking."

Ying Chanxi shook her head, her thoughts a mystery. After Li Luo got his food, she took out her own meal card and placed it on the card reader.

"What are you doing?" Li Luo was taken aback for a moment.

"I'm in a good mood, can't I be?"

Li Luo smiled and didn't refuse. "Then I won't be polite."

After a free meal, they all returned to the classroom together.

Once the lunch break was over, they rushed to the sports field's spectator stands to watch the afternoon competitions.

Although Li Luo had only signed up for the 3000-meter as an individual event, he was actually participating in several team events as well.

For instance, the afternoon's 4x100-meter relay included him.

Unfortunately, the first event in the afternoon was the 400-meter race, which both Zhang Guohuang and Lin Yuan participated in, consuming some of their stamina.

Although there was about an hour's rest in between, it still slightly affected their performance in the 4x100-meter relay, and they barely managed to secure eighth place in the end.

At least they got one point.

After the relay race, according to the student council's arrangement, Li Luo had to go get busy at the gymnasium again.

At this moment, Zhu Yufei shouted toward the stands, "Yan Zhusheng, Wang Xinyu, your high jump event is coming up."

According to the rules for the First Affiliated High School's sports meet, a student could sign up for a maximum of three individual events, of which a maximum of two could be track and field events.

Team events were not included in this limit; students could sign up for as many as they wanted.

As for student-athletes, they were restricted to signing up only for the one event they were best at and regularly competed in; they could not participate in any other events.

"This must be fate," Li Luo said, standing up with Yan Zhusheng and sighing. "I happen to be in charge of guiding the high jump contestants to the field."

"Weren't we allowed to choose our tasks during the meeting?" Shi Yanran, sitting in the back row, said in confusion. "Class President, did you remember wrong?"

Li Luo: "...My dear Youth League Secretary, although I highly approve of your work ethic, it seems you still have a lot of room for improvement when it comes to social skills and worldly wisdom."

Yan Zhusheng looked at Shi Yanran, then at Li Luo, and said nothing. But instead of walking down the steps one by one as she normally would, this time she hopped down the steps of the stands.

After reaching the bottom, she tilted her head up to look at Li Luo, signaling him to hurry up and follow.

Li Luo put his hands in his pockets, yawned, and slowly followed behind. Wang Xinyu, on the other side, also hurried over, and the three of them walked toward the gymnasium.

Perhaps having heard some rumor, Wang Xinyu's gaze shifted between Li Luo and Yan Zhusheng, and she silently maintained a distance from the two of them.

Once they arrived at the gymnasium, Li Luo reported to the gym teacher, awaiting his instructions.

Just then, a familiar voice reached his ears.

"Li Luo, Zhusheng." Ying Chanxi waved at them as she walked over from the gymnasium entrance, then looked at Li Luo with suspicion. "How come it feels like you're always here leading the group whenever Zhusheng is competing?"

"Don't you go spouting nonsense, I wasn't here when she ran the 200-meter," Li Luo corrected her. "Besides, during the 100-meter race this morning, I was leading your group, alright?"

"Is that so..."

"So why are you here?" Li Luo looked at Ying Chanxi. "The 1500-meter hasn't started yet, has it?"

"I'm here with Xinyan for her competition," Ying Chanxi said, pointing at Qiao Xinyan beside her. "She's also participating in the high jump."

"Huh?" Li Luo looked at Qiao Xinyan, sizing her up and down. "Little Yanzi knows how to high jump?"

"Don't look down on people!" Qiao Xinyan stood on her tiptoes and raised a fist, though in reality, her head only reached Li Luo's chin.

Ying Chanxi, however, blinked, stepped closer to Li Luo, gestured twice at his chest, and asked with a puzzled look, "Have you grown taller recently?"

"I think so," Li Luo recalled. In his past life, his height had shot up starting from the second year of middle school, and by the time he graduated, he was already 175 cm.

By the end of his first year of high school, he had reached a little over 180 cm, after which his growth stagnated. By the time he graduated high school, he was about 183 cm.

It was already mid-November, so he had probably grown a little taller.

He hadn't felt it himself, but Ying Chanxi had keenly noticed the change.

"Qiao Xinyan, Yan Zhusheng..." The gym teacher started calling names for check-in. Hearing their names, Yan Zhusheng and Qiao Xinyan obediently walked over.

Ying Chanxi took half a step back and sighed.

"What's wrong?"

"Nothing, just a little nervous," Ying Chanxi said, glancing at the competition schedule posted on the nearby bulletin board. "After the high jump and long jump this afternoon, it's the 1500-meter. I heard there are student-athletes participating."

"We're not aiming for a top rank or anything. Just finishing the race is a success," Li Luo comforted her. "If it comes to it, I can run with you."

"Really?"

"Why would I lie to you?"

"Maybe not. You still have the 3000-meter tomorrow."

"You're overestimating your abilities. Running the 1500-meter with you would probably just be a warm-up exercise for me."

"How dare you look down on me?!"

After some playful banter, Li Luo led the team to the high jump competition area.

As Yan Zhusheng demonstrated the absolute advantage of her long legs on the field, Li Luo, standing on the sidelines, said to Ying Chanxi, "If you're still nervous, I have an idea."

"What idea?"

"It's a secret for now." Li Luo smiled. "When your race is about to start, remember to prick up your ears and listen carefully."

"Huh?" Ying Chanxi didn't understand what Li Luo meant and was completely baffled.

But after the high jump competition ended, Li Luo waved at her and returned to the Class Eight stands with Yan Zhusheng.

It wasn't until four-thirty in the afternoon.

Zhu Yufei said from the stands, "Jin Yuting, Xiuxiu, you two get ready. The 1500-meter check-in is about to start."

"Okay, got it." Xiuxiu, who had been diligently studying her English vocabulary list, closed her book.

Lin Yuan, at her side, had already folded up the sun umbrella. He extended his hand, took the vocabulary list from Xiuxiu to put it away, and twisted open a bottle of water to hand to her. "Have some water."

"Oh... thank you."

"Eww," Zhang Guohuang rubbed his arms, feeling goosebumps all over. After Xiuxiu and Jin Yuting had left, he couldn't help but imitate Lin Yuan's tone, speaking softly to Zhu Yufei next to him, "Xiuxiu, have some water."

"Mmm, thank you, Yuanyuan," Zhu Yufei responded in a pinched voice, playing along perfectly.

"Damn it!" Lin Yuan felt his own goosebumps rising and kicked at them through the air, flustered and exasperated. "We didn't sound nearly as sickening as you two just now!"

Li Luo watched the antics of these clowns with a laugh, checked the time, then patted his pants and stood up, heading toward the rostrum.

He grabbed a guitar from backstage, found Xu Youyu, and smiled at her. "Senior Sister, I've come to contribute another piece."

"You bring a guitar to contribute a piece?" Xu Youyu glanced at the guitar in his hand and asked with a look of suspicion, "Are you sure it's just a contribution?"

"Ahem." Li Luo coughed and said in a low voice, "And to sing a song, to cheer on our schoolmates."

"Is that so." Xu Youyu looked at him with a wide smile. "I recall there's a women's 1500-meter race coming up."

"Just say if you'll allow it or not!"

"According to regulations, only the two hosts and the school leaders can use the microphone."

"So?"

"A month of cleaning duty at home."

"One week."

"Half a month, no less. I'm taking a risk here too, you know."

"Deal!" Li Luo said through gritted teeth. "And to think I cut your cleaning duty in half before. I really misjudged you."

"It's fine. If you perform well, I might reduce it for you too," Xu Youyu said with a grin. "Let's go, the microphone is yours. If you need anything, you can tell the people in the backstage broadcast room."

"No needs, just stop the music in a bit," Li Luo said, patting the guitar in his hands. "And get me a microphone for the guitar too."

A few minutes later, on the rostrum, everything was ready.

The host next to them looked at Xu Youyu. Seeing the president nod, he recited the lines they had just prepared into the microphone:

"With spirits soaring and youth surging, some students run and leap on the field, while others work and support silently behind the scenes."

"Student Li Luo from Class Eight, Year One, also the guitarist of the rock music club, was inspired after participating in the sports meet and would like to present a song for everyone. The song is titled—'Light'."

Just as the students in the stands were listening to the announcement in surprise, the sports meet's background music had already stopped.

The entire field suddenly fell into a quiet atmosphere.

The next second, the rhythm of a guitar slowly began to play.

Many people looked toward the rostrum and saw Li Luo's figure.

By now, Li Luo had brought his lips close to the microphone and began to sing softly:

"Can't see the light they say is on the other side"

"Could it be just a figment of imagination"

"Is it that I don't believe enough in heaven"

"So I don't deserve to hope"

Hearing Li Luo's voice, Ying Chanxi, who was in the gymnasium preparing to check in for the 1500-meter race, was first stunned. Then, leaving Qiao Xinyan who had accompanied her, she bolted out of the gymnasium doors.

She stood at the entrance, gazing from afar at the figure on the rostrum. The unfamiliar melody and familiar voice filled her ears, leaving her momentarily transfixed.

(End of this chapter)
